children: Fairfax Financial sold its whole stake in Indian lender IIFL Finance for about $370mn on November 18, raising cash for its $5.66bn takeover of state-controlled IDBI Bank.
The Canadian insurer's unit FIH Mauritius Investments offered more than 56mn shares at a floor price of INR611 ($6.54), 3.9% below the previous close,
The Times of India
reported. The block was worth about INR34.54bn, a person with direct knowledge of the trade told
Reuters
, and IIFL Finance shares climbed as much as 6.5% on the day.

Money is moving across Asia's borders into banks, and most of it is heading for India. In the same two days Japan's Daiwa Securities Group set out plans to grow in China and South Korea's Kakao Bank bought into a Mongolian lender. Both are spending profits earned in unusually strong home markets.

Foreign stakes in Indian lenders, deal value, $bn. Rupee values converted at November 18, 2026 ECB reference rates. Source: Government of India; Emirates NBD and RBL Bank; Reuters; The Indian Express. IntelliNews
A strike that did not stop the sale

New Delhi's Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on October 15 cleared the sale of 60.72% of IDBI Bank to a Canadian subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings for INR528.78bn, or INR81 a share. The government is selling 30.48% and Life Insurance Corporation of India 30.24%, and officials expect the deal to be the biggest foreign direct investment yet in India's financial sector. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must still judge the buyer fit and proper.

IDBI's staff unions want the deal scrapped. The United Forum of IDBI Officers & Employees held a two-day nationwide strike on November 2 and 3, calling the valuation inadequate and the process opaque, the
Indo-Asian News Service
reported. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has argued that the sale breaches RBI rules limiting a foreign owner to 26% of the voting rights in an Indian bank.
The queue of foreign buyers

Fairfax would be the largest of several foreign buyers. Emirates NBD took 60% of RBL Bank on June 18 through a primary share issue worth about $2.75bn, which the two lenders described as the first purchase of a majority stake in a profitable Indian bank by a foreign bank, according to their joint statement. The Dubai bank's own Indian branches merge into RBL on December 1.

Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp paid INR134.83bn for 20% of Yes Bank, and Bank of America agreed in August to take up to 49.9% of Jio Credit, the lending arm of Jio Financial Services, for as much as INR182.68bn.
The books these buyers are paying for are much cleaner than a decade ago. Non-performing loans at Indian banks fell to 2.1% of gross loans in 2025 from 10% in 2017, according to World Bank data.
Indian banks' non-performing loans, % of gross loans. Source: World Bank (IMF Financial Soundness Indicators) via IntelliNews Lambda
Japan and Korea push outwards
Daiwa intends to expand cross-border M&A, listings and advisory work in China now that it owns all of its mainland securities venture,
Nikkei Asia
reported on November 18. Daiwa agreed in April to buy the 49% held by two Beijing state-owned partners for CNY706mn,
Bloomberg
reported at the time. 'We are the only Japanese brokerage with an investment banking license in China,' Zhu Hongxia, Daiwa's deputy head for Asia and Oceania, told the newspaper.

In Seongnam, south of Seoul, Kakao Bank on November 17 signed for 15% of M Bank, the digital lender of Mongolian conglomerate MCS Group, and became its second-largest shareholder. No price was disclosed. Mongolia is the Korean internet bank's third foreign market, after a stake in Indonesia's Superbank in 2023 and a holding in Thailand's planned virtual lender Bank X.
Paid for at home

Japan's three megabanks all raised their targets for the year to March 2027 on November 13. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group lifted its net profit goal to JPY2.8 trillion ($17.5bn) from JPY2.7 trillion and authorised a buyback of up to JPY200bn. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group raised its forecast to JPY1.9 trillion ($11.9bn) from JPY1.7 trillion and added a JPY220bn repurchase. Mizuho Financial Group now expects JPY1.6 trillion, up from JPY1.4 trillion.

Each figure is above the record each group earned in the year to March 2026, when MUFG made JPY2.43 trillion, SMFG JPY1.58 trillion and Mizuho JPY1.25 trillion. Higher domestic interest rates have widened lending margins, and the groups are fighting over wealthy clients at home as well.
Japan's megabanks, net profit attributable to owners of parent, JPY trillion. Source: MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho results filings. IntelliNews

Those earnings, and the Gulf's, give lenders the capital to keep shopping abroad, and India remains the main destination. Whether the IDBI strike and the political objections can slow the flow will become clearer once the RBI rules on Fairfax.

title: Foreign banks keep buying into India
